literal: Xiu would rather die this morning than be mocked by posterity.
idiomatic: Xiu would rather die today than be a laughingstock tomorrow.

literal: Hun's attendants all changed color and trembled with fear; Xiu's expression was calm as before.
idiomatic: Hun's men blanched and shook; Xiu's face never changed.

literal: Hun and his wife fell silent, nursing resentment.
idiomatic: Hun and his wife said nothing, swallowing their rage.

literal: Another day he wrote on the arm of Chief Medical Attendant Yang Huifu the characters "old slave official stingy," and had him show it to Xiu.
idiomatic: Another day he had "old-slave-official-stingy" written on Chief Medical Attendant Yang Huifu's arm and shown to Xiu.

literal: Hun always sought an opening to trap him.
idiomatic: Hun kept watching for a chance to ruin him.

literal: When Hun was executed in secret, Xiu thus escaped disaster.
idiomatic: When Hun was put to death in secret, Xiu escaped.

literal: At the time Xiu and Chief Counselor Gao Yun of Bohai, both esteemed as Confucian elders, were heavy in reputation.
idiomatic: Xiu and Bohai's Chief Counselor Gao Yun were both famed Confucian elders of the day.

literal: Both were selected for regional posts, but because of inquiries and consultations were kept at court; each was allowed to send his eldest son out as prefect of a commandery.
idiomatic: Both were slated for provincial office but kept at court for consultation; each was allowed to send his eldest son out as commandery prefect.

literal: Xiu firmly declined and would not accept; permission was granted.
idiomatic: Xiu firmly declined; the court allowed it.

literal: From beginning to end he served five emperors.
idiomatic: From first to last he served five emperors.

literal: Though he never reached the highest offices, he was constantly at the pivot of state affairs.
idiomatic: He never held the highest rank but was always at the heart of affairs.

literal: Upright, pure, and frugal, he did not amass property.
idiomatic: Upright, pure, and spare—he built no fortune.

literal: At age seventy-three he fell ill; an edict provided physicians and medicine and granted folding stool and staff.
idiomatic: At seventy-three he fell ill; the throne sent doctors and medicine and granted staff and folding stool.

literal: When the court's actions and great matters were unresolved, they often sent Vice Director Li Fu of Pingyang, Marquis of Gaoping, to his residence for decisions.
idiomatic: When court action or a great matter stalled, Vice Director Li Fu, Marquis of Gaoping, was often sent to his house for a ruling.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Governor of Jizhou, Duke of Wuyi, posthumous name Jian (Simple).
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of Jizhou, Duke of Wuyi, posthumous name Simple.

literal: His son Jun, styled Yilin.
idiomatic: His son Jun, styled Yilin.

literal: Inherited the title, post of Governor of Jingzhou, reduced to marquis per regulation.
idiomatic: He inherited the title, served as Governor of Jingzhou, and was reduced to marquis by rule.

literal: Earlier Shangluo had been set as Jingzhou, later changed to Luozhou; among heavy mountains people did not know learning — Jun memorialized to establish school officials.
idiomatic: Shangluo had once been Jingzhou, later Luozhou; in the deep mountains learning was unknown—Jun petitioned to set up school officers.

literal: Five years in the province, pure and quiet with few affairs, the officials and people were at ease under him.
idiomatic: Five years in office, pure and quiet, little business—the clerks and people were at ease.

literal: At death posthumously Governor of Yanzhou.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Governor of Yanzhou.

literal: His son Shuxiu inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Shuxiu inherited.

literal: Run's great-grandson Zhen, styled Shuyuan, steeped in classics and histories, famed for filial piety in mourning.
idiomatic: Run's great-grandson Zhen, styled Shuyuan, steeped in the classics and histories, famed for mourning his parents.

literal: In the Taihe era, as Doctor of the Secretariat accompanying Vice Director of the Secretariat Gao Cong to Jiangzuo.
idiomatic: In Taihe he went as Secretariat doctor with Vice Director Gao Cong to the lower Yangzi.

literal: On return, because his mother was old and ill he promptly stayed home to attend her and was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: On return his mother was old and ill; he stayed home to nurse her and was removed from office.

literal: Later Secretariat Consulting Staff Officer, Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded, with supernumerary title Champion General.
idiomatic: Later he was Secretariat consulting officer, Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded, with supernumerary rank Champion General.

literal: At death posthumously Governor of Qizhou.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Governor of Qizhou.

literal: Zhen's brother's son Jingjun was also famed for learning, as Outside Military Staff Officer to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
idiomatic: Zhen's nephew Jingjun was also known for scholarship, outside military staff officer to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

literal: Yu raised rebellion in Jizhou and was about to appoint him;
idiomatic: Yu rebelled in Jizhou and was about to give him a post;

literal: he would not accept and died for it.
idiomatic: he refused and died for it.

literal: Posthumously Governor of Hedong, posthumous name Zhen (Upright).
idiomatic: Posthumously Governor of Hedong, posthumous name Upright.

literal: Jingjun's younger brother Jingyu, pure stern and upright, was chief clerk of a province and then lingered without taking office.
idiomatic: Jingjun's younger brother Jingyu, stern and upright, was a provincial chief clerk and then would not serve.

literal: Later when Ge Rong took Jizhou he claimed illness and would not bow.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong seized Jizhou he pleaded illness and would not bow.

literal: Jingyu would stroke his knee and say: "I have not failed you."
idiomatic: Jingyu would pat his knee and say, "I have not failed you."

literal: — for not bowing to Rong.
idiomatic: — for refusing to bow to Rong.

literal: Dou Jin, styled Daoyu, native of Weiguo in Dunqiu, descendant of Han Minister of Works Dou Rong of Yunhan.
idiomatic: Dou Jin, styled Daoyu, of Weiguo in Dunqiu, descended from Han Minister of Works Dou Rong.

literal: Gao ancestor Cheng, Administrator of Dunqiu, made it his home.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cheng, Administrator of Dunqiu, settled the family there.

literal: Jin from youth was famed for letters; from Doctor of the Secretariat to Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed Viscount of Fanyang.
idiomatic: Jin was famed young for letters; from Secretariat doctor to vice director, enfeoffed Viscount of Fanyang.

literal: Participated in state counsels with repeated merit, advanced to Marquis of Weiguo, transferred to Director of Four Departments.
idiomatic: He took part in state planning with repeated merit, rose to Marquis of Weiguo, then Director of Four Departments.

literal: When the Three Qins were first pacified and people still wavered, appointed Regional Commander of Chang'an, Duke of Piling.
idiomatic: When the Three Qins were first settled and allegiance still shifted, he was made Regional Commander of Chang'an, Duke of Piling.

literal: Eight years in the command, very distinguished in authority and kindness.
idiomatic: Eight years in command—his authority and kindness were renowned.

literal: Summoned as Director of Palace Attendants and of the Capital Ministries.
idiomatic: He was summoned as Director of Palace Attendants and Capital Ministries.

literal: Emperor Taiwu personally favored him and rewarded him lavishly.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu favored him personally and rewarded him richly.

literal: On campaign against Gai Wu; when Wu was pacified, Jin was left to garrison Chang'an.
idiomatic: On campaign against Gai Wu; when Wu fell, Jin was left to hold Chang'an.

literal: Back in the capital again as Director within the palace and of capital ministries, in charge of law enforcement at the emperor's side.
idiomatic: Back in the capital he again directed palace and capital ministries and held law at the emperor's side.

literal: Taiwu sighed: "The state's good assistant — that means the Duke of Piling."
idiomatic: Taiwu sighed: "The state's true pillar is the Duke of Piling."

literal: Out as Governor of Jizhou, pure and abstemious, famed at the time.
idiomatic: Sent out as Governor of Jizhou, pure and spare—famed in his day.

literal: Returned as Grand Director of Palace Officials.
idiomatic: He returned as Grand Director of Palace Officials.

literal: In the first year of Xingguang, Jin's son-in-law Moduo, marshal of Prince of Yulin, was selected to marry Princess of Linjing; Jin taught Moduo to decline.
idiomatic: In Xingguang 1 Jin's son-in-law Moduo, marshal to Prince of Yulin, was chosen for Princess of Linjing; Jin urged Moduo to refuse.

literal: On pretext of slander and curse words, he was executed together with Moduo; only the youngest son Zun escaped by hiding.
idiomatic: On charges of slander and cursing he was executed with Moduo; only the youngest son Zun hid and lived.

literal: Zun excelled in regular and seal script; northern capital steles and tower-pavilion palace gate inscriptions were mostly Zun's writing.
idiomatic: Zun excelled in regular and seal script; most northern-capital steles and palace gate inscriptions are his.

literal: Post of Administrator of Puyang, much accepting bribes.
idiomatic: As Administrator of Puyang he took many bribes.

literal: His son Sengyan fornicated with another man's wife; reported by local man Jia Miao, dismissed from office.
idiomatic: His son Sengyan lay with another man's wife; Jia Miao of the district reported him and he was dismissed.

literal: Later because of fine calligraphy made Director of Storehouses, died in office.
idiomatic: Later, for fine calligraphy, he was made Director of Storehouses and died in office.

literal: Li Xin, styled Yuansheng, childhood name Zhennu, native of Fanyang.
idiomatic: Li Xin, styled Yuansheng, childhood name Zhennu, of Fanyang.

literal: Great-grandfather Chan, Chan's son Ji — both generations famed under the Murong.
idiomatic: Great-grandfather Chan and Chan's son Ji—two generations famed under the Murong.

literal: Father Chong, Minister of Civil Service and Administrator of Shicheng under Feng Ba.
idiomatic: His father Chong was Minister of Civil Service and Administrator of Shicheng under Feng Ba.

literal: When the imperial carriage reached Helong, Chong led more than ten commanderies to submit; Taiwu greatly honored him, calling him Lord Li.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Helong, Chong led more than ten commanderies to submit; Taiwu honored him greatly and called him Lord Li.

literal: Governor of Northern Youzhou, Marquis of Gu'an.
idiomatic: Governor of Northern Youzhou, Marquis of Gu'an.

literal: At death posthumous title Marquis Xiang.
idiomatic: At death his posthumous title was Marquis Xiang.

literal: Xin's mother was low-born and was slighted by his elder brothers.
idiomatic: Xin's mother was of humble birth and his elder brothers looked down on him.

literal: Chong said: "At this child's birth diviners said he would be noble; each time I look, perhaps it cannot be known."
idiomatic: Chong said, "At his birth the diviners said he would be noble; each time I look I still cannot tell."

literal: So he sent him to the capital as student of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: So he sent him to the capital as a Secretariat student.

literal: Taiwu visited the Secretariat school, saw him and thought him unusual, pointed and told followers: "This boy will in the end be useful to my descendants."
idiomatic: Taiwu visited the Secretariat school, saw him, thought him unusual, and said to his attendants, "This boy will one day serve my house."

literal: So he took special notice of him.
idiomatic: So he marked him for special notice.

literal: The emperor's uncle Duke of Yangping Du Chao had a daughter to be given to a noble house; the emperor said: "Li Xin will surely reach high office and benefit another's gate — she can be wife to him."
idiomatic: The emperor's uncle Duke of Yangping Du Chao had a daughter for a noble match; the emperor said, "Li Xin will surely rise and enrich another house—give her to him."

literal: So he urged the marriage.
idiomatic: So he pressed the marriage.

literal: The southerner Li Zhe often said Xin would surely reach noble eminence.
idiomatic: The southerner Li Zhe often said Xin would surely reach high rank.

literal: When Du Chao died the emperor himself mourned three days.
idiomatic: When Du Chao died the emperor mourned him in person for three days.

literal: Xin as Chao's son-in-law was able to come and go in mourning quarters.
idiomatic: As Chao's son-in-law Xin could enter and leave the mourning hall.

literal: The emperor pointed and said to attendants: "Watch this man's bearing — is it not unlike the crowd?"
idiomatic: The emperor pointed him out and said, "Look at this man's bearing—is it not unlike the crowd?"

literal: He will surely be a capable minister for my house.
idiomatic: He will surely be a pillar of my house.

literal: Xin was quick, clever, argumentative, with strong memory and sharp perception.
idiomatic: Xin was quick, clever, sharp-tongued, with a strong memory and keen eye.

literal: Initially Li Ling was Wencheng's erudite; edict for Cui Hao to select the best students of the Secretariat school as assistant teachers.
idiomatic: At first Li Ling was Wencheng's erudite; an edict had Cui Hao pick the best Secretariat students as assistant teachers.

literal: Hao nominated his disciple Son Xiang, Lu Duanshi, and Li Fu — three to respond.
idiomatic: Hao named his pupil Son Xiang, Lu Duanshi, and Li Fu.

literal: Gaoyan's son You and Duan Ba's nephew and others said Hao showed favoritism to kin, told Jingmu.
idiomatic: Gaoyan's son You and Duan Ba's nephew and others said Hao favored kin and told Jingmu.

literal: As Hao was unfair, it reached Taiwu.
idiomatic: The charge of unfairness reached Taiwu.

literal: Taiwu had Xin in mind and said: "Why not take old man Li Chong's son of Youzhou?"
idiomatic: Taiwu had Xin in mind and said, "Why not take old Li Chong's boy from Youzhou?"

literal: Hao replied: "Earlier I also said Xin fit selection, but because he was first traveling outside, was not taken."
idiomatic: Hao said, "I said Xin fit before, but he was away and was not taken."

literal: The emperor said: "Can wait for Xin to return and dismiss Xiang and the others."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wait until Xin returns and dismiss Xiang and the rest."

literal: So made assistant teacher and erudite of Secretariat, entered to teach Wencheng the classics.
idiomatic: He was made assistant teacher and Secretariat erudite and taught Wencheng the classics.

literal: Wencheng acceded; Xin for old favor was intimate and favored, promoted Master of Rites, concurrently head of Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed Duke of Fufeng.
idiomatic: When Wencheng took the throne Xin, for old favor, was intimate and favored—Master of Rites, head of the Imperial Secretariat, Duke of Fufeng.

literal: His mother Lady Sun was enfeoffed Lady of Rongcheng.
idiomatic: His mother Lady Sun was made Lady of Rongcheng.

literal: The emperor told the ministers: "In the year I first studied I could not concentrate;
idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "When I first studied I could not fix my mind;

literal: having assumed all affairs there was hardly leisure to warm old lessons.
idiomatic: once I held all affairs I had no leisure to review old lessons.

literal: Thus in truth the Confucian way had gaps — not only my fault
idiomatic: So the Confucian way truly had gaps—not mine alone

literal: but also the teachers' lack of diligence.
idiomatic: but also my teachers' slackness.

literal: Therefore rank and reward remain lofty — I do not forget the old."
idiomatic: Therefore rank and reward stay high—I do not forget the old days."

literal: Xin doffed cap and bowed in thanks.
idiomatic: Xin removed his cap and bowed in thanks.

literal: Out as Governor of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Xiangzhou.

literal: His government was pure and simple; the common people praised him.
idiomatic: His rule was pure and simple; the people praised him.

literal: Xin memorialized asking that each province and commandery establish school officials so men of local standing and gentry scions could come to study.
idiomatic: Xin petitioned that every province and commandery set up schools so local worthies and gentry sons could study.

literal: Those penetrating in the classics would go up to the princely mansions.
idiomatic: Those who mastered the classics would enter the princes' households.

literal: The memorial was submitted; Xianwen approved.
idiomatic: The memorial went up; Emperor Xianwen approved.

literal: Because Xin's governance was the best among the provinces, extra robes were granted.
idiomatic: Xin's governance was judged best among the provinces and extra robes were granted.

literal: From then on he had a proud, self-satisfied air, accepting people's goods and merchants' treasures.
idiomatic: From then on pride took him; he took people's goods and merchants' treasures.

literal: Soldiers reported it.
idiomatic: Soldiers reported him.

literal: Vice Director Li Fu and Xin had been close from youth; Fu always shielded him.
idiomatic: Vice Director Li Fu and Xin had been close since youth; Fu always covered for him.

literal: Some urged reporting to the throne; Fu would not allow it.
idiomatic: Some urged reporting to the throne; Fu forbade it.

literal: Xianwen heard of Xin's crimes, sent a caged cart to summon Xin, and tortured him to establish guilt.
idiomatic: Xianwen heard of Xin's crimes, summoned him in a cage-cart, and tortured him to conviction.

literal: The Fu brothers were about to be cast off; the authorities hinted at the inner will's dislike of the Fu brothers and had Xin report and list Fu's hidden crimes so he could save himself.
idiomatic: The Fu brothers were to be cast aside; the authorities hinted at the throne's dislike and told Xin to denounce Fu's hidden crimes to save himself.
